claims.content: Retrieve published RLCS status (lane status, customer access, sign messages) from an external server outside the RLCS network.

goal.raw_text: Retrieve published RLCS status (lane status, customer access, sign messages) from an external server outside the RLCS network.

claims.content: External Traffic System
The RLCS Application must be operational and maintaining current status for all devices at each controller unit.
External systems shall retrieve RLCS status from a server outside the RLCS network (outside a firewall).

The external communications interface to the Department of Transportation ISSC resource (possibly via WAN) must be active, as this is the one-way output-only interface through which external systems access RLCS data.
An external traffic system initiates a request to retrieve RLCS status data from the external server via the Department of Transportation ISSC resource interface.

trigger.raw_text: An external traffic system initiates a request to retrieve RLCS status data from the external server via the Department of Transportation ISSC resource interface.

claims.content: The External Traffic System initiates a connection to the Department of Transportation ISSC resource via the one-way output-only interface.
The system accesses RLCS data through the external server located outside the RLCS network (outside a firewall).

The system retrieves a single data file containing the following data elements: Status (e.g., open northbound, open southbound, closed), Customers (e.g., RLCS/FasTrak only, all traffic), Access (e.g., location 1 open, location 2 closed), and Signs (e.g., Sign 1 'Express Lanes Open', Sign 2 'Express Lanes Closed').

If the primary connection to the Department of Transportation ISSC resource is unavailable, the External Traffic System may utilize a secure remote dial-in interface through a firewall via a dial-up modem.
The alternative dial-in interface allows connection into the RLCS network via a remote computer equipped with the application software, requiring a user logon authorized for remote access.

If the connection to the Department of Transportation ISSC resource fails or is unavailable, the system may attempt to connect via the secure remote dial-in interface through a firewall using a dial-up modem.

If the External Traffic System attempts to use the dial-in interface without being equipped with the application software or lacking an authorized user logon for remote access, the connection into the RLCS network will be denied.
The External Traffic System has successfully retrieved the single data file containing RLCS status elements (Status, Customers, Access, Signs).
The retrieved data includes Status information (e.g., open northbound, open southbound, closed).
The retrieved data includes Customer information (e.g., RLCS/FasTrak only, all traffic).
The retrieved data includes Access information (e.g., location 1 open, location 2 closed).
The retrieved data includes Sign messages (e.g., Sign 1 'Express Lanes Open', Sign 2 'Express Lanes Closed').
